name: Abbie Hoffman
role: American activist, Yippie co-founder and Chicago Seven defendant (1936–1989)
summary: Hoffman co-founded the Youth International Party and used theatrical stunts to oppose the Vietnam War and the established order. He rejected reform in favour of revolution and a leaderless society of free goods, backed street trashing and property destruction, and later campaigned against nuclear power.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He testified that Woodstock Nation holds that people should have better means of exchange than property or money.

abortion-legal.rationale: Steal This Book says free abortions must be looked on as a fundamental right and praises the pressure of radical women for liberalised laws.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Steal This Book thanks the Viet Cong and treats the US invasion of Vietnam as genocide against a nation of great vision.

automate-paid-work.rationale: He testified that the work ethic made no sense because within a few years machines would do all the work anyway.

direct-action.rationale: In 1969 he said the right to change the system by voting was destroyed, but by 1980 he fought a local nuclear plant through committees and wanted Ted Kennedy as president.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Steal This Book describes the free society it demands as one where technology produces goods and services for whoever needs them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He described himself as a cultural revolutionary shaping a new style of living through art, theatre and music, and called fun subversive.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In 1969 he said that when a black man demands his constitutional rights it is called violent, and that Bobby Seale being gagged and chained in court symbolised four hundred years of treatment of black people.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In 1980 he said he fought a nuclear plant in his valley and said 'we need to tear down the plants now', with no phase-out programme.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: In 1980 he said the 1960s struggle succeeded because US troops are no longer fighting in Nicaragua, Latin America, Africa or Iran, and that the cause continues until they stay home.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Steal This Book says its chapter headings (free food, medical care, housing, transport, education) spell out the demands for a free society.

free-public-college.rationale: Steal This Book lists free education among the demands for a free society and explains how to get a college education free.

gradual-change.rationale: Asked what reforms he supports, he answered that he supports none: reform implies a sound system and he believes in revolution.

legalize-drugs.rationale: In 1980 he called making cocaine illegal a political decision by racist bigots and called it a beneficial stimulant when used properly, and he criticised censorship.

multipolar-world.rationale: In 1980 he said no one force is supposed to rule the world or 'own the whole enchilada', whether the USA or the USSR.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Steal This Book says whether its methods are legal or illegal is irrelevant because the dictionary of law is written by the bosses of order.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He testified that the aim was a situation in which people take part and become their own leaders; in 1980 he said problems must be worked out by the people from the bottom up.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: In 1980 he said every politician and candidate is a liar and accused one of putting political ambition ahead of friendship and of elitism.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Steal This Book teaches street fighting, bombs against property and calls trashing 'revolutionary violence', while telling readers to avoid injuring people and to phone in warnings.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: Steal This Book says institutional violence manipulates values and mores to keep the power of the few, and that the dictionary of law is written by the bosses of order.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Steal This Book says freedom of the press belongs to those who own the distribution system, and that printing your own book is not real press freedom in a mass society.

production-for-use.rationale: Steal This Book's demand is a community where technology produces goods and services for whoever needs them, not for profit-making institutions he calls corporate feudalism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Steal This Book calls it immoral not to steal from the institutions of the 'Pig Empire' and says bank robbers rather than bankers should run universities, while forbidding theft from comrades.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: Steal This Book advises as much property destruction as possible against banks, corporations, federal buildings and police stations, and sets out bombs aimed at empty buildings.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Steal This Book says America was built on the slaughter of a people and that the Indians should have defeated the whites in the films.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He said the system had abridged the constitutional right to amend it by voting and, quoting Lincoln, that the people have a revolutionary duty to overthrow that government.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: In 1969 he said he does not believe in reform or dissent but in revolution, and that people have a duty to overthrow the system.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: He rejected reform and dissent in favour of overthrowing the system rather than working within established institutions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Steal This Book says its aim is not to fuck the system but to destroy it; in 1969 he called the system archaic, immoral and brutal and said it must be overthrown.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Steal This Book states that laws, cops and courts exist to protect the power and property of those who already have it.

state-harmful.rationale: Asked what government he would have after the revolution he answered 'no government', and he saw the government as withering in the shuffle; the answer was partly a joke.

strong-leader.rationale: He testified that the Yippies had no concept of leadership, that people should be their own leaders, and described a leaderless society.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: He called the law under which he was tried rigged and unconstitutional, and Steal This Book treats legality as irrelevant to the moral duty to act.

vanguard-party.rationale: He testified that the Yippies rejected leaders and wanted every person to be their own leader, which is the opposite of a disciplined leading party.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: He testified that the Yippies rejected values that keep people in a rat race of work and postponed pleasure, calling fun a rebuttal.

youth-equal-civil-rights.rationale: In 1969 he called curfews and ID checks on young people fascism.

notes: Searched by theme in Steal This Book (the one book in the local library), his 1969 trial testimony, a Nov. 1969 radio interview, a Feb. 1980 High Times interview and a 1968 speech. Elections, courts, religion, gender, immigration and most economic statements found no stated position. His views are mostly stated in the 1968–72 period; the 1980 interview shows continued opposition to US intervention and a turn to local environmental organising.
